text:
anya: Heads-up — I found KMS-wrapped ciphertext blobs in staging logs from the partner ingestion pipeline. Not plaintext creds, but the wrapped blobs include our KMS key ID. Could be partner misconfig or they sent us pre-wrapped artifacts.

mike: Can you paste an example log line?

anya: Sure — grep output:
```
2026-02-18T14:02:03Z INFO ingest: source=partner-x file=upload-20260218.json kms_ciphertext=CiQA... key_id=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/partner-ring/cryptoKeys/wrap-key
```

cory: If the wrapped blob references our key, we need to treat it as potential exposure of key usage metadata. Action items: limit partner SA write scope to a temp queue and rotate wrapping key if partner can't rewrap quickly.

jamie: Also we should stop logging the full upload body. The pipeline currently logs the object payload on non-200 for debug — that's probably how these blobs showed up. I'll open a patch to filter object payloads.

security-oncall: Important: ciphertext-only doesn't mean compromise of plaintext. But procedural containment is required: 1) confirm no unwrapped secrets landed anywhere, 2) revoke partner SA write perms to ingestion path, 3) rotate wrapping key, 4) request partner to re-encrypt with new key or use an ephemeral exchange.

mike: I'll take owner on partner comms. Proposed immediate steps I can run now:
- block partner SA: `gcloud projects remove-iam-policy-binding redwood --member=serviceAccount:partner-sa@partner.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/storage.objectCreator`
- deploy logging filter (jamie pls)
- create new KMS key version and revoke old: `gcloud kms keys versions create --key=wrap-key --keyring=partner-ring --location=global` (then disable old version)

cory: FYI if we disable the old version, any existing ciphertext we have becomes undecryptable until partner rewraps (or we rewrap via transit). We should coordinate a window where partner will re-encrypt or we run a rewrap job. Consider using Vault Transit to do a controlled rewrap if needed.

jamie: Patch ready: small change to ingestion logger to drop `object_payload` and replace with `object_size` and `kms_key_id`. PR: https://github.com/redwood/ingest/pull/812 — will request an emergency review.

security-oncall: Please also forward relevant audit logs to SIEM and snapshot them. Need: storage ACL changes, KMS admin operations, vault transit calls. If SIEM forwarding isn't already capturing all, add an ad-hoc export.

anya: I checked SIEM — we have object create logs but not every downstream service call. I'll export the last 7 days of storage and KMS admin logs and drop in the secure incident bucket.

mike: Partner outreach draft: "Partner team — we observed uploads referencing our wrapping key. Please stop sending wrapped artifacts until we coordinate key rotation. We'll provide a new wrap key or a rewrap endpoint. Contact: mike@redwood.com" Will send once RBAC block is in place.

cory: Suggest we create a short-lived rewrap endpoint using vault transit with an ACL: only allow partner SA to submit ciphertext for rewrap and return new ciphertext with our new key. That avoids them handling raw plaintext. Consider rate limits and auditing.

jamie: RBAC change checklist I'm doing:
- create IAM binding rollback plan (terraform)
- add conditioned role for `roles/storage.objectCreator` limited to `resource.name.startsWith("projects/_/buckets/partner-ingest")`
- enable org policy to prevent logging object payloads in staging

security-oncall: I've opened an incident ticket to track this: INC-2026-1234. Assigning roles: mike=partner comms, jamie=RBAC & logging patch, cory=KMS/rewrap plan, anya=evidence collection.

sre-bot: deploy status: ingest logger patch (PR #812) merged to hotfix, build started, deploy to staging blocked pending security review.

anya: Quick note — partner says they don't have decryption keys on their side for these blobs (they thought they were sending opaque artifacts). We need to treat it as protocol mismatch, not exfil. Still rotate keys.

mike: OK sending partner note after RBAC block. Timeline: block now, logging filter live in 30m, key rotation tomorrow 02:00 UTC, rewrap window 02:30–04:00 UTC. Is that OK?

security-oncall: Approved timeline. Make sure to capture key version numbers before rotation and keep an offline record for recovery. Also record who requested rotation in audit ticket.

cory: I'll prepare a step-by-step rewrap runner (k8s job) and an idempotent script:
```
# rewrap-runner (concept)
kubectl run rewrap-job --image=rewrap:latest --env NEW_KEY=projects/redwood/.../new-wrap-key
# job reads blob from staging-queue, calls vault/transit:rewrap, writes to secure-queue
```

jamie: After rollout, we'll run a brief smoke test to ensure ingestion + replay works and no decryption failures. I'll coordinate with QA.

anya: Thanks all. I'll attach exported logs to INC-2026-1234 and mark as evidence. Mike, ping when partner confirms readiness for rewrap.

security-oncall: Closing signal: once new key version is active, partner re-encrypted backlog completed, SIEM shows no unwrapped plaintext access, and RBAC filters are live. Then we'll downgrade incident severity.

mike: On it. Will update thread as we progress. :thumbsup:
